명령 한 줄의 여정: The journey of one command line
COMMIT은 정말 디스크에 썼을까?: Did COMMIT really write to disk?
주문 1042번을 결제 완료로 바꾸고 <code>COMMIT;</code: You change order 1042 to "paid" and type COMMIT;. About 1 ms later, Commit complete. appears.
데이터파일은 수십 GB이고, 바꿀 블록은 그 안 어딘가에 있습니다. 그: The data files are tens of GB, and the block to change is somewhere inside them. Did it really write all the way there in that short time? Let's follow one SQL statement.
커밋은 데이터파일을 고치는 일이 아닙니다. 무엇을 바꿨는지 적은 짧은 기: A commit is not the act of fixing the data file. It is the act of leaving a short record of what changed on disk.
먼저 블록을 메모리로 가져온다: First, bring the block into memory
서버 프로세스는 디스크의 행을 직접 고치지 않습니다. 먼저 행이 들어 있: The server process does not change the row on disk directly. It first looks for the 8 KB block holding the row in the SGA's Buffer Cache.
캐시에 없으면 데이터파일에서 블록을 읽어 옵니다. 이것을 물리적 읽기라고: If the block is not in the cache, it is read from the data file. This is called a physical read.
같은 블록을 다시 쓰면 메모리에서 바로 찾습니다(논리적 읽기). 자주 쓰: When the same block is used again, it is found straight in memory (a logical read). The longer frequently used blocks stay in the cache, the less the disk is read.
값을 바꾸기 전에 Oracle은 원래 값 <code>'NEW'</code: Before changing the value, Oracle creates Undo information holding the original value 'NEW'. Undo goes into blocks of an undo segment, and those blocks are also in the Buffer Cache. The undo block is actually changed in the next step, together with the data block, while generating redo.
Undo는 두 가지 일을 합니다. <code>ROLLBACK</code>: Undo has two jobs. On ROLLBACK it restores this value, and when another session reads this row it shows the row as it was before the commit.
다른 세션은 내가 커밋하기 전까지 'NEW'를 봅니다. 잠금이 풀리기를: Until I commit, other sessions see 'NEW'. They do not wait for the lock to be released; they build the old image from Undo and read it. This is read consistency.
이번 변경은 두 군데입니다. 데이터 블록(<code>'NEW'</code: This change touches two places: the data block ('NEW' → 'PAID') and the undo block. Oracle turns each change into a change vector, puts them into the Redo Log Buffer, and changes both blocks. In the words of Concepts 19c, "a redo record contains both the change to the data block and the change to the undo block."
고친 블록은 이제 디스크 내용과 다릅니다. 이런 블록을 <span cla: The changed block now differs from what is on disk. Such a block is called a dirty block. The data file is still unchanged.
Redo에는 Undo 블록의 변경도 들어갑니다. 그래서 장애가 나도 Re: Redo also includes the change to the undo block. So even after a failure, Redo alone is enough to rebuild Undo as well.
서버 프로세스는 새 <span class=\"term\">SCN</spa: The server process gets a new SCN (system change number) 8104230 and puts a commit record into the Redo Log Buffer.
그리고 백그라운드 프로세스 <span class=\"term\">LGWR: Then it wakes the background process LGWR and waits until the write is reported finished. This wait is the wait event log file sync.
커밋하는 순간에도 데이터 블록은 메모리에만 있습니다. 디스크로 가는 것은: Even at the moment of commit, the data block is only in memory. Only Redo goes to disk.
~ 세션: log file sync 대기: ~ Session: waiting on log file sync
LGWR은 버퍼에 쌓인 Redo를 <span class=\"term\">: LGWR appends the Redo accumulated in the buffer to the end of the online redo log file. Appending to the end of a file is a fast sequential write, and when many sessions commit at once they are written together in one go.
쓰기가 끝나면 LGWR이 서버 프로세스에 알리고, 그제야 화면에 <cod: When the write finishes, LGWR notifies the server process, and only then does Commit complete. appear on screen. It usually takes around 1 ms, depending on the storage.
LGWR은 커밋 때만 쓰지 않습니다. Concepts 19c에 따르면 3: LGWR does not write only at commit. According to Concepts 19c it also writes every 3 seconds, when the Redo Log Buffer is one-third full or holds 1 MB, at a log switch, and before DBW writes dirty blocks. So Redo from before the commit may already be on disk, and at commit only the remaining Redo has to be written.
커밋이 보장된다는 것은 Redo가 디스크에 있다는 뜻입니다. 지금 전원이: A guaranteed commit means the Redo is on disk. Even if the power goes out now, this change survives.
데이터파일은 나중에 몰아서 쓴다: Data files are written later, in batches
dirty 블록은 커밋 뒤에도 한동안 메모리에 남습니다. <span cl: Dirty blocks stay in memory for a while even after the commit. DBWn writes many blocks together to the data files later, when a checkpoint comes or free buffers run short.
규칙이 하나 있습니다. 블록을 데이터파일에 쓰기 전에 그 블록의 Redo: There is one rule. Before a block is written to the data file, that block's Redo must already be on disk. This is called write-ahead logging.
데이터파일 쓰기는 흩어진 위치에 하는 랜덤 쓰기라 느립니다. 이 일을 커: Writing data files is slow because it is random writing to scattered locations. Commits are fast because this work was taken out of the commit path.
사례: 커밋 직후 서버가 꺼졌다: Case: the server went down right after the commit
커밋은 끝났지만 DBWn이 블록을 쓰기 전에 전원이 나갔습니다. SGA는: The commit finished, but the power went out before DBWn wrote the block. The SGA is gone, and the data file still holds 'NEW'.
다시 시작하면 <span class=\"term\">SMON</span>: On restart, SMON performs instance recovery. It first reads Redo and reapplies every change since the last checkpoint (roll forward), then rolls back uncommitted transactions using Undo (roll back).
커밋된 'PAID'는 Redo 덕분에 돌아오고, 커밋하지 않은 변경은 사: The committed 'PAID' comes back thanks to Redo, and uncommitted changes disappear. Because Redo exists, it is safe to postpone writing the data files.
사례: 한 건마다 COMMIT 하는 배치: Case: a batch that COMMITs every row
주문 100만 건을 처리하는 배치 프로그램(Java, JDBC)이 한 건: A batch program (Java, JDBC) that processes one million orders sends an UPDATE and a COMMIT for each row. A COMMIT sent by a client defaults to WRITE WAIT IMMEDIATE (SQL Language Reference 19c), so every commit waits for LGWR's write. Even at just 1 ms each, the waiting alone comes to about 1,000 seconds, close to 17 minutes.
AWR 보고서에서는 <code>log file sync</code>가 상: In the AWR report, log file sync rises to the top wait events. If you commit once at the end of each business unit of work, for example every 5,000 rows, the number of commits drops to 200.
같은 반복을 PL/SQL 블록 안에서 하면 사정이 다릅니다. PL/SQL: Doing the same loop inside a PL/SQL block is different. According to the PL/SQL Language Reference 19c, PL/SQL's default commit behavior is BATCH NOWAIT (when COMMIT_LOGGING and COMMIT_WAIT are not set), so it does not wait for the write on every row, and the calculation above does not apply. You can also remove the wait on the client with COMMIT WRITE NOWAIT, but a failure can lose changes you just committed, so use it only for data you can afford to lose.
정리: 커밋은 Redo가 디스크에 닿는 순간: Summary: a commit is the moment Redo reaches disk
UPDATE는 Buffer Cache의 블록을 고치고, 그 변경을 Und: UPDATE changes the block in the Buffer Cache and records the change in Undo and Redo.
COMMIT은 Redo만 디스크에 쓰고 돌아옵니다. LGWR이 파일 끝에: COMMIT writes only Redo to disk and returns. It is a fast sequential write that LGWR appends to the end of the file.
데이터파일은 DBWn이 나중에 모아서 씁니다. 그 사이에 장애가 나도 R: DBWn writes the data files later, in batches. Even if a failure happens in between, Redo recovers it.
